summary: S.J. Res. 91 is a joint resolution that uses the Congressional Review Act to officially disapprove and cancel a Bureau of Land Management rule from December 9, 2024. That rule established a record of decision for the Coastal Plain Oil and Gas Leasing Program in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge, which had set aside about 1.2 million acres as unavailable for leasing while keeping the statutory minimum of 400,000 acres available.

affected_groups.effect: Impacted by the removal of the rule that restricted leasing to a smaller portion of the Coastal Plain program area in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge.

key_provisions: Nullifies the Bureau of Land Management rule issued on December 9, 2024, relating to the Coastal Plain Oil and Gas Leasing Program Record of Decision.
Declares that the nullified rule shall have no force or effect.
Targets the decision that replaced the 2020 record of decision and adopted Alternative D2 from the 2024 supplemental environmental impact statement.
Eliminates the restriction making approximately 1.2 million acres unavailable for oil and gas leasing and exploration.

summary_detail.plain_summary: S.J. Res. 91 is a joint resolution that uses the Congressional Review Act to officially disapprove and cancel a Bureau of Land Management rule from December 9, 2024. That rule established a record of decision for the Coastal Plain Oil and Gas Leasing Program in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge, which had set aside about 1.2 million acres as unavailable for leasing while keeping the statutory minimum of 400,000 acres available.
summary_detail.significance: The resolution carries legislative significance by attempting to overturn a specific federal administrative rule concerning oil and gas leasing in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge, though the latest recorded action shows it was indefinitely postponed by the Senate by unanimous consent.
